limitations: Ordinary non-forced reads retain the existing successful-content TTL; a shared deadline enables eligible forced retry rather than promising a new collection on every read.
A running collection still coalesces requests. Exact-deadline request assertions require an idle service and an otherwise eligible company.
No new immediate cross-view propagation, provider expansion, cache-format changes or initial-progress latency work.
Unanimous approval is a phase decision, not a defect-free product guarantee.
The browser evidence is limited to the eleven selected Chromium E2E files in development and production, with one worker and zero retries; it is not a complete browser-suite or cross-browser run.
Provider responses and saved records are synthetic. No live-company availability rate, external API load, production traffic or distributed collector behavior is measured.

Exact one-millisecond retry and freshness boundaries, legacy persisted records, daily-source gates and both-direction null/short retry floors are primarily unit evidence; real-server browser tests use observed timestamps from a running fixture clock.

Status reaches an existing exploration view when the app receives a catalog response. A still-fresh view does not automatically receive a saved-page presence result; the real-server test explicitly reloads before expecting that state.

Ordinary non-forced reads keep the existing successful-body TTL. Passing a shared retry deadline permits otherwise-eligible work rather than requiring a body request on every read, and active collections still coalesce requests.

The real-server fixture observes upstream and HTTP completion events. Its instrumentation has a footprint; its measured retry window is evidence for the synthetic execution, not a production latency benchmark.

The production fixture compares the served entry JavaScript with its copied build. The runner also checks the complete local build manifest before and after production E2E; this is not an audit of every served asset response.

Fable independently verified source, contract and plan hashes through its read-only identity helper. Four execution-control hashes were cross-referenced against the preserved control receipts rather than freshly recomputed by Fable; Main freshly checked the control files, Astra reviewed the controls and unchanged deltas, and the runner verifies controls at execution boundaries.

Source/control endpoint hashes and the cooperative validation lock cannot exclude an external edit-and-restore. Requested model effort is recorded, but the Fable backend does not independently expose its effective effort setting.

All-three approval is a decision to accept this stage's recorded evidence and limitations, not a guarantee that the product has no defects. Failed runs and unreachable assertions remain distinct from final successful runs.

Detailed logs, reports, browser/runtime copies, traces and screenshots are temporary. They are reviewed before cleanup; reusable tools, decisions, result summaries and hashes are preserved in Git first.
